text:
Amy: heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I'm seeing a ~30% p99 increase for short/burst text requests (batch size 1-4). repros attached, looks like fallback to generic kernel for certain sequence lengths :thinking_face:
Devin: ugh, thanks. do you have a perf profile or example trace? can you dump kernel_choice tag from the traces? :eyes:
Amy: yeah uploading profile snippet now. main curious bit is when token_len ~56 we pick kernel A, but for 57 we fall back to generic and latency jumps. copying raw flame:```
flame: kernel_A (3.2ms) -> kernel_generic (12.8ms)
queue_wait: 0.4ms
kv_cache_lookup: 0.1ms (miss)
```
Raj: that pattern matches an older heuristics change i made (heuristic: prefer fused kernels if seq_len % 16 == 0). maybe new model tokenization shifted distribution. can you paste example input lengths and which model variant?
Amy: model: gte-small-v1, input lens seen in logs: [52, 56, 57, 64], route: /v1/generate:small. sample log: `kernel_choice=generic seq=57 reason=fallback-no-fused`
Olivia: also noticed increase in KV cache miss rate for those exact requests on the same route — could be padding/aligning changed. if cache miss happens we lose KV speedups which amplifies kernel delta. i've got a short query to get per-route kv-hit/miss by seq len for the last 24h.
Devin: OK two action items: (1) add `kernel_choice` and `seq_len_bucket` tags to token-level latency metric so dashboards can split, (2) correlate kv_hit boolean and kernel_choice to get joint distribution. Can we add those without high cardinality explosion?
Raj: propose seq_len_bucket with coarse buckets [1-32,33-64,65-128,129+], kernel_choice set to {fused_A,fused_B,generic,quant_fast}. kv_hit is boolean. that should keep cardinality manageable.
Amy: +1. also want per-route `unit_cpu_ms_per_token` derivation so we can compute cost per token by kernel. currently billing lines only get token counts and route, not kernel.
Olivia: i can join that — from infra we can emit an aggregate per-minute metric: `tokens_by_kernel{route,kernel_bucket}` and `cpu_ms_by_kernel{route,kernel_bucket}`. then Optimize can map to billing using price-per-cpu-ms and token-counts.
Devin: can we backfill for the last 7 days (sampled traces) so we can compute delta in unit economics pre/post-change? we need data for customer impact and to decide rollback.
Raj: infra-bot should have sampled traces. @infra-bot can you run a 7d sample query for traces where route=/v1/generate:small and seq_len in [48..72] and include kernel_choice + kv_hit?
infra-bot: Automated run queued — query id q_2026_07_12_001. will post summary CSV to #eng-platform in ~10m. :gear:
Amy: great. also adding a small repro patch: i can try forcing kernel preference override (env REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFER=fused_A) to validate root cause. will spike a canary with 2% traffic.
Devin: please do canary. also add a tiny dashboard widget: token-level latency waterfall that layers `queue`,`kv_lookup`,`kernel_exec` by kernel_choice. that should make regressions obvious. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Olivia: will own dashboard changes + emitting `tokens_by_kernel` metric. Raj — can you change selector heuristics to avoid hard mod-16 boundary? maybe use latency-estimate table per-seqlen computed from offline profiling.
Raj: yup. i'll prototype a small lookup table; fallback threshold only if expected_gain > 2x. should be safe.
Amy: thanks all. let's aim to have canary + dashboard in next 3 hours and backfill CSV first. I'll report results in this thread. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: q_2026_07_12_001 complete — uploaded: s3://redwood-infra/q_2026_07_12_001.csv (summary attached).
Devin: got it, looking now. initial glance: kernel_choice shifts explain ~28% of the p99 delta and kv-miss explains another ~6%. sending quick query results in a follow-up message.
Amy: perfect. will wait for the follow-up before rolling any rollback.
Devin: follow-up: query shows tokens_by_kernel for route `/v1/generate:small` over 48-72 len window: `fused_A: 42% tokens, generic: 38% tokens (pre-change 12%)`. estimated cpu_ms_per_token: fused_A=1.6, generic=6.4. cost implication: roughly 3-4x cost on affected tokens.
Raj: that's large — good we caught it in canary. i'll push a quick heuristic revert and the lookup table patch to avoid the sharp boundary. will notify when deployed.
Olivia: dashboard PR opened: https://git.redwood.company/p/redwood/dashboards/pulls/234 — includes waterfall widget + `tokens_by_kernel` panel + `unit_cpu_ms_by_kernel`.
Amy: thanks — seeing infra-bot csv and PR. keeping thread open until canary shows numbers back to baseline.
Devin: one last ask: add `billing_token_label` to metrics pipeline so downstream billing can attribute extra cost to kernel anomalies for reconciliation with customers if needed.
Olivia: noted, adding to pipeline schema.
Raj: rollback patch deployed to canary 2% -> kernel_choice distribution matches pre-change. monitoring now.
Amy: canary looks good after 15m: p99 back to baseline for that route. will run a 1h canary before full revert.
infra-bot: canary metrics: p99 latency delta for /v1/generate:small = +0.8% (within noise).
Amy: excellent. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a short postmortem and an instrumentation ticket to make kernel_choice and kv_hit permanent tags. :white_check_mark:
